children: Earnings season delivered several contrasting signals, from
Nvidia’s
blockbuster artificial intelligence demand to
Walmart’s
more cautious weight-loss drug outlook. Investors also weighed cloud growth, cybersecurity spending and driverless technology.

Across the reports, companies exceeded expectations in key areas while highlighting risks ranging from U.S. chip restrictions to rising investment costs. Here are five stories that shaped this week’s market conversation.
Nvidia’s AI Demand Accelerates
NVIDIA Corp.

reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, surpassing the $109.08 billion analyst estimate, according to Benzinga Pro. Adjusted earnings reached $2.68 per share, above expectations of $2.48. The report marked the company’s first without founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down last week.
Alibaba’s AI Gains Face Chip Pressure
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.

shares rose after the Chinese e-commerce company posted mixed second-quarter results. Artificial intelligence and cloud computing are becoming increasingly important growth drivers, although softer e-commerce demand, higher capital spending and tighter U.S. chip restrictions cloud the outlook.
Walmart’s Weight-Loss Boost Fades
Walmart Inc.

shares declined in Thursday’s premarket trading despite stronger-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results and another increase to its full-year outlook. Adjusted earnings came in at 65 cents per share, ahead of the 64-cent estimate, excluding a 3-cent after-tax loss tied to equity and other investments.
Palo Alto Expands Beyond Cybersecurity
Palo Alto Networks Inc.

reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $3.45 billion, exceeding the $3.31 billion analyst forecast. Adjusted earnings totaled $1.05 per share, beating the 97-cent estimate, according to Benzinga Pro. The cybersecurity company also announced an acquisition of Applied Compute.
Pony AI’s Driverless Business Gains Ground
Pony AI Inc.

reported better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, supported by rapid expansion in its Robotaxi and Robotruck operations. Quarterly revenue increased 75% year over year, while operating expenses climbed just 3%, indicating that the company’s driverless business is growing faster than its spending.

title: Nvidia's AI Demand, Alibaba's Chip Pressure and More: This Week in Tech
